correctness.rationale: Assessed the full repaired RESULT.md. The frozen Finding at line 9 literally said the signed infinitesimal-delay slope increases strictly; the allowed T_2<T_1 makes this false, although the frozen proof correctly uses its magnitude. The repair changes that finding to the magnitude statement, states the two signed directions, and identifies the known mean-circulation comparison by equation. Indeed Delta'_u(0+)=(T_2-T_1)u/(k+u) has coupling derivative k(T_2-T_1)/(k+u)^2; its absolute value increases strictly and has no finite maximizer. The two principal coupling optima need no change. The stationary centered normal modes have positive drift rates k and k+2u; their stationary cross covariance is (T_1-T_2)/(2(k+u)). Propagating each mode and returning to particle coordinates yields the stated sign and difference of exponentials. At fixed u, the derivative in lag vanishes exactly once at log(1+2u/k)/(2u), a global maximum of the magnitude. With x=2u/k the integral is proportional to h=x/((x+1)(x+2)) and the peak to h(1+x)^(-1/x). The area derivative has sign 2-x^2. The peak log derivative has sign F=(x+2)log(1+x)-x^2, with F(0)=0, F'(0)>0, F''=x/(1+x)^2-2<0 and F tending to minus infinity. Thus there is one positive peak optimum; F(2)>0 places it strictly above sqrt(2). Independent bisection and substitution reproduced x*=2.223254940100293 and both reported magnitudes and coupling ratios. The temperature gap is a positive prefactor so cannot affect either optimizer; equal temperatures are properly excluded. Reassessment of the repaired finding finds both optima and their corrected short-time comparison valid under the stated hypotheses.
residual_risks: No optimization result is inferred for equal temperatures, unequal stiffnesses or mobilities, nonharmonic dynamics, or nonstationary data. Numerical bisection corroborates the constants but is not the uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: Delayed asymmetry can be read either as the largest lagged signal or as signal accumulated over lags. Comparing these natural objectives in the same model shows quantitatively that changing the way lags are summarized changes the unique optimal coupling, while the magnitude of the instantaneous comparator has no finite optimum. This is useful as a benchmark for finite-delay observables; metric dependence is not captured by a stationary solution or the classic circulation formula alone. The repair preserves that contribution and removes a misleading signed statement.
residual_risks: The result is model-specific and does not optimize measurement noise or a finite-sample estimator; no experimental effect is inferred outside the specified OU dynamics.
